author: agent
question: Can a coding agent run as one small binary with no hidden cuts?

points.claim: It is one static binary with four tools, reading and writing plain text.
points.spoken: It is one static binary with four tools, and it reads and writes plain text.
points.source_note: README: one 7 MB static binary, four tools, plain stdin/stdout
points.title: One binary

points.claim: The whole conversation is sent on every call, and file output is never truncated.
points.spoken: The whole conversation goes out on every call, and file output is never cut short.
points.source_note: README: entire conversation sent each call; output never truncated
points.title: Lossless by default

points.claim: It has no screen interface, no telemetry, no plugins and no automatic retries.
points.spoken: It has no screen interface, no telemetry, no plugins and no automatic retries.
points.source_note: README: deliberately no TUI, telemetry, plugin system, automatic retries
points.title: What it leaves out

points.claim: It works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local servers.
points.spoken: It works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including servers you run on your own machine.
points.source_note: README: provider neutral; OpenAI-compatible; local servers; resumable sessions
points.title: Any compatible model

catch: It never compacts context, so a long session stops at the provider's limit.
catch_sub: The harness exits with an error instead.
cta: Would you run a coding agent in a pipeline? Comment UNCUT and I'll pin the repo link.

youtube.title: UNCUT: A Coding Agent in One Small Binary
youtube.description:
UNCUT is a lossless, headless coding agent harness: one static binary, four tools, plain stdin and stdout. It sends the whole conversation on every call, never truncates file output, and exits with an error rather than passing off a partial answer.
Repo: https://github.com/Balanov/uncut
